findings.claim: ACR uses one stimulus judged independently: integers 1 bad, 2 poor, 3 fair, 4 good, 5 excellent. KonIQ uses this technical-quality scale. Mean ratings can be fractional; preserving raw votes permits histograms, mean and disagreement estimates.

SPAQ uses continuous 0–100 overall quality, higher better, with five verbal quality regions. Its attributes are separate 0–100 brightness, colourfulness, contrast, noisiness and sharpness. Attributes are not interchangeable quality components: high noisiness is worse, high colourfulness or contrast is not automatically better. Raters are explicitly told to focus on quality rather than aesthetics; at least 15 ratings/image.

A direct HD-video experiment with 24 viewers per condition and 128 processed videos found no significant overall differences between five-point discrete, nine-point discrete and continuous scales after rescaling. This does not prove equivalence for our photo/teacher pipeline. More numeric bins alone do not establish more precision.

Five verbal grades are ordered categories. Treating their numeric codes as equally spaced is a modelling convention, not a physical measurement fact. National response styles and category thresholds can differ. MOS is relative to a study and viewing protocol; it is not a percentage of photographic perfection.

KADID shows a reference and distorted image, using degradation categories: 5 imperceptible, 4 perceptible but not annoying, 3 slightly annoying, 2 annoying, 1 very annoying. Official file dmos.csv is [1,5], higher better. Do not invert it merely because the column is named DMOS.

LIVE collected raw 1–100 quality ratings, then formed each reference rating minus distorted-image rating, removed outliers, computed per-subject z-scores, and applied cross-session scale realignment. Published DMOS is higher worse. Realigned values need their documented observed range; do not assume nominal raw 1–100 bounds survive processing or clip them without an explicit policy.

AVA measures aesthetic preference with scores 1–10 and raw distributions; 78–549 votes/image, mean 210. Its mean alone loses consensus information. Aesthetic appeal and technical quality should remain separate targets, even where they correlate. Photo contest judgements are not a neutral technical quality scale.

Putting all datasets into [0,1] or [0,100] does not align perceptual quality. Even independent sessions on the same LIVE collection required realignment. Options include common human-rated anchors and monotonic mappings, dataset-specific heads/mappings, or within-source ranking objectives. Do not construct cross-source ranking pairs solely from rescaled MOS.

KonIQ tested scalar and distribution targets. MSE on scalar MOS was marginally best in-domain; Huber on rating distributions was best cross-tested on LIVE-in-the-Wild (0.836 SROCC). Retaining distributions is valuable, but does not prove a distribution head/loss always wins.

Record raw human votes, rater count, sample SD and bootstrap confidence interval for the mean when justified. SD describes disagreement; standard error/CI describes estimate precision. Teacher repeat spread and token distributions are model-derived uncertainty, not human vote counts or human confidence intervals.

MOSAIQ-500K proposes common-scale mapping of 23 IQA datasets using 919 images and 36,760 retained ratings from 40 subjects. It collects 0–100 technical-quality ratings and fits monotonic mappings. Useful corroboration and future candidate; inspected paper says code/data will be made public upon acceptance. Its inclusion of AVA does not prove aesthetic and technical constructs equivalent.

recommendation.confidence: High for separate constructs, explicit score direction, raw provenance and calibration; moderate for selecting five-level raw collection over a continuous slider.
recommendation.human_labels: For a new broad-photo reference set, collect technical_quality_grade in {1,2,3,4,5} with named ACR anchors and fixed viewing instructions. Collect aesthetic_appeal_grade separately only if this product axis remains in scope; five grades for a consistent new rubric are a project choice, not the native AVA protocol. Preserve every vote. Compute mean_1_5 and distribution rather than rounding the aggregate.
recommendation.canonical_values: Use continuous 1–5 per target as the canonical score, with human integer votes retained separately. Derived training value q01=(score_1_5-1)/4 and optional 0–100 display 25*(score_1_5-1) are exact unit conversions. They add no information and are not cross-dataset calibration. Preserve original source value, bounds, direction, study and aggregation metadata.
recommendation.teacher_values: A direct continuous 1–5 score in tenths is a provisional teacher protocol to compare with named five-level grades on held-out human data. Tenths are an output precision choice, not demonstrated perceptual resolution. If using five-level token logits, retain logits/probabilities and derive expected score, but label it model-derived. Never call self-reported probability a measured human distribution. Do not mechanically bin continuous specialist predictions when the raw value can be retained.
recommendation.scope_gate: Missing, unreadable, ineligible and abstained observations use explicit status plus null score, not zero. Diagram/render controls should train domain eligibility separately; source identity does not justify a low technical-quality or aesthetic label.
recommendation.core_test: Before bulk labelling, compare the proposed five-level and continuous teacher protocol against a stratified human reference set, evaluating ordering and calibrated error on the same processed views. This is a calibration experiment, not a guarantee of training success.
recommendation.strongest_counterargument: A five-class output collapses differences needed for fine ranking when only one teacher vote is retained. SPAQ and MOSAIQ demonstrate viable continuous ratings. We should preserve continuous specialist predictions and human means, and test five-level expectations versus direct continuous teacher scoring rather than declaring a universal winner.
recommendation.unresolved_gap: We have no task-specific human calibration evidence showing that our chosen teacher distinguishes subtle defects, respects intentional blur, separates aesthetics, or orders near-ties better on five versus continuous scales. Source protocols cannot settle that locally.

decision.primary_targets: Separate continuous technical/perceptual quality and aesthetics scalars. Keep source human votes, source MOS/variance, teacher outputs and scale provenance as distinct records.
decision.canonical_scale: Continuous1–5 is a defensible common application scale; a display0–100 is derived as25*(score1to5-1). Choice of numeric range does not itself add signal.
decision.human_collection: For new discrete human ratings, bad=1, poor=2, fair=3, good=4, excellent=5. Preserve all votes and count; compute mean/variance later. A slider protocol is a separate explicitly versioned alternative.
decision.generic_teacher: Keep current anchored1–5 tenths as a provisional elicitation arm, not a claim of0.1 accuracy. Compare it with five verbal levels plus real token logprobs on the human calibration set before bulk promotion. Do not switch all master labels to hard ordinal solely because Q-Align uses words.
decision.specialist_teacher: Preserve continuous expectation and, where available, the five actual level-token logits/probabilities. Adapter MUST name checkpoint revision, API entry point, token order, weights, preprocessing and output range.
decision.optional_distribution: Use empirical human vote distributions or provenance-labelled model token distributions. Never relabel a JSON-elicited probability vector as human vote uncertainty or token softmax. Do not fabricate human variance from an isolated scalar.
decision.qalign_adapter: Equal-width five-bin conversion is legitimate in a separately versioned Q-Align replication arm. It is NOT nearest-integer rounding or the original human vote. For[1,5], Q-ReAlign boundaries are1.8,2.6,3.4,4.2, with4.2 entering excellent. Retain the scalar master target.
decision.compact_student: Start with separate scalar heads and masked losses; optional empirical distribution supervision/ordinal EMD only where reliable targets exist. Add within-source or calibrated pairwise ranking after pointwise baseline; do not equate uncalibrated cross-dataset MOS.
decision.certainty: High confidence that IQA and IAA should remain separate and continuous source information should be preserved; moderate confidence in exact generic-teacher1–5 tenths prompt until measured on the target views and human gold.
decision.promotion: Teacher validation must be task-specific: success on IQA does not qualify it for aesthetics. Five-level convention does not prove current general API model has calibrated quality probabilities.

models.name: Q-Align / OneAlign
models.supervision: Continuous dataset MOS is converted to five equal-width word classes; next-token cross entropy. Distinct task prompts for quality, aesthetics and video.
models.inference: Restricted softmax of five level-token logits, weighted expectation. Paper and HF AutoModel use[5,4,3,2,1] ->[1,5]. Current GitHub QAlignScorer uses[1,.75,.5,.25,0] ->[0,1].
models.evidence: Original Table11 compares level-trained vs direct-score-trained mPLUG-Owl2. It supports that training recipe, not a universal superiority of hard ordinal collection or zero-shot prompts.
models.quality: Original paper, authors' implementation and checkpoint code; direct API range discrepancy verified.

models.name: Q-ReAlign
models.supervision: Q-Align-style five word labels for IQA/IAA/VQA. map_score normalizes source range then bins floor(t*5); optional DMOS direction inversion.
models.inference: Default names excellent,good,fair,poor,bad; weights1,.75,.5,.25,0. Current scorer appends answer stem, extracts next-position logits and softmaxes the five first token IDs.

prompt_examples.iqa: How would you rate the quality of this image?
prompt_examples.iaa: How would you rate the aesthetics of this image?

models.caveat: Model card calls scores dataset-conditioned and asks recalibration before mixing scales. Token matching uses first token; adapter must validate correct, distinct tokens for chosen tokenizer.
models.quality: Authors' executable source and official HF model card; model card benchmark claims not reproduced.

models.name: DeQA-Score
models.supervision: Five-bin soft target from human MOS and standard deviation, Gaussian discretization with expectation/mass adjustment; fallback adjacent-bin interpolation for very small variance. Soft loss plus within-dataset Thurstone fidelity relationships.
models.label_fields: Source generator preserves gt_score, gt_score_norm, level_probs, std, std_norm.
models.findings: Hard one-hot quantization loses mean precision, boundary relationships and uncertainty. Paper shows identical linearly rescaled scores can still have different perceptual meanings across studies; within-dataset ranking addresses this.
models.caveat: Gaussian labels are a fitted representation from human statistics, not raw vote histograms or self-reported model confidence. Source generator uses observed dataset extrema; do not blindly inherit this preprocessing in a held-out production protocol.
models.quality: CVPR paper, original distribution generator and inference implementation; no reproduction.

models.name: NIMA
models.supervision: Predict a ten-bin rating distribution with ordered Earth Mover's Distance loss. AVA aesthetic bins1–10; TID2013 technical bins0–9. When raw distributions unavailable, reconstruct by maximum entropy using MOS and std.
models.inference: Expected rating and standard deviation from distribution.
models.findings: Technical and aesthetic models share architecture but train on different target datasets. It does not train one merged quality+aesthetics label. Ratings and source scale remain task-specific.
models.caveat: A synthetic model-provided distribution is not an empirical histogram. Number of bins is a representation choice and does not establish100-point annotations are better.
models.quality: Original author paper read through HF markdown and Exa excerpts.

models.name: Q-Insight
models.supervision: GRPO with score-regression reward plus degradation type and intensity rewards. Needs MOS and defect labels, not labelled reasoning chains.
models.inference: Official demo asks a float1–5 rounded to two decimal places in JSON rating, with generated reasoning.
models.findings: Joint defect training improves sensitivity to subtle faults such as JPEG. Direct numeric generation can work after task-specific RL, providing counterevidence to a blanket prohibition on scalar targets.
models.caveat: Two decimal formatting is not evidence of0.01 perceptual accuracy; task-trained results do not validate an unadapted generic teacher prompt.
models.quality: Original paper substantive search passages, official demo code and HF model metadata.

models.name: LEAF
models.supervision: Frozen InternVL3.5-8B provides five-word token-logprob expectation1–5; pair A/B decisions from token logprobs; reliability1-H(p)/log2. ConvNeXt student learns SmoothL1 point targets plus weighted pairwise BCE. Human MOS calibration uses MSE+PLCC.
models.findings: Supports compact scalar scorer and final human calibration; pairwise-only did less well than pointwise+pairwise in paper ablation. Pair number approximately dataset size, not all pairs.
models.caveat: Preprint; inspected text says code will be released on publication. Prompt appendix was referenced but absent from fetched main body, so exact unobserved templates are not claimed. Token entropy is not proof of error calibration.
models.quality: Author preprint methods and ablations; lower reproducibility confidence than released source-backed methods.

models.name: VisualQuality-R1
models.supervision: Generates multiple1–5 scalar scores, computes within-batch comparative probabilities from means and sample variances under Thurstone, and trains with fidelity rewards derived from human preference.
models.inference: Scalar1–5 after reasoning; not simply an A/B ranking classifier.
models.findings: Ranking-aware training handles relative quality and mixed study scales. Paper explicitly reports high inference cost and risk of confidently wrong reasoning.
models.caveat: Training target is a ranking relationship, but published model still emits numeric scores. Does not require our compact deployed student to generate reasoning.
models.quality: Original paper methods, ablations and limitations.

models.name: RALI
models.supervision: Q-Insight generates image-text-score triples; freeze text encoder, contrastively adapt CLIP vision encoder to quality text, compress features and score with quality-labelled prototypes.
models.inference: Weighted prototype-score scalar; prototype score artifacts determine output range. Demo uses softmax similarity weights and learned prototype scores.
models.findings: Supports avoiding a large reasoning model at deployment. Distilled brief quality descriptions may be useful later as auxiliary supervision.
models.caveat: Paper reports approximately4% of Q-Insight parameter/time cost in its setup; not a performance guarantee for our data or EmbeddingGemma. Does not justify broad mandatory descriptions in v1.
models.quality: Original paper plus released inference implementation; benchmark claims not reproduced.

recommendation.status: Proposed protocol, not experimentally proven best.
core_constructs: Technical image quality: perceptual impairment of visible image information under fixed display/view conditions.
Aesthetic appeal: visual composition, colour/light use and overall visual impact; a separate judgement.
Photo-domain eligibility: suitability for the intended real-world-photo collection; a policy/coverage decision, not an IQA score.

anchors.1: Bad: severe impairment; essential visual information is largely lost.
anchors.2: Poor: major visible defects substantially reduce clarity.
anchors.3: Fair: noticeable defects, but the main content remains adequately visible.
anchors.4: Good: minor defects with little effect on perceived clarity.
anchors.5: Excellent: no material defect visible in the specified view.

aesthetics_level.priority: separate secondary target, initially validate on human calibration subset

anchors.1: Very weak visual organisation or impact.
anchors.4: Strong, coherent and pleasing visual presentation.
anchors.5: Exceptional visual presentation and impact within the stated photo scope.

photo_domain_eligible.note: Use null for unresolved scope. Known charts/renders are false for a real-photo corpus. This field is not a claim about AI origin inferred from pixels.

per_axis_status.note: Every null score needs a reason. Errors and absent evidence never become low scores.

derived_scores.note: Keep original individual ordinal ratings and counts. A display conversion adds no measurement precision. If product requires 1–100 use 1+99*q01 explicitly; avoid ambiguous mappings.

edge_cases: A sharp but dull photograph can receive high technical quality and ordinary aesthetics.

A deliberate soft-focus portrait, shallow depth of field, film grain or motion treatment is not automatically a technical failure. Judge whether visible detail is impaired where it matters; do not claim hidden artistic intent.
A black-and-white or low-key image is not automatically a colour/exposure defect; judge visible loss of required information.
A valid, severely damaged photograph must receive a low technical score rather than be removed as unscorable merely for looking bad.
Unreadable bytes or failed model requests get null with error, never quality zero.

Charts/renders can be excellent within their own domains. For a photo-only scorer, mask photo quality/aesthetics as out_of_scope and set photo eligibility false; an application may reject them with a separate utility score of zero.
Known AI-generated origin is provenance. Do not silently equate AI-generated, visually implausible, nonphotographic, low aesthetic and poor technical quality.

Blank controls require an explicit scope rule: either rate a decoded blank as extreme visual failure under a broad quality target, or treat it as out_of_scope for a photo-only target. Do not mix those conventions without an explicit target definition.
Do not call a single model rating a human MOS, and do not treat self-reported confidence or prompted probabilities as observed rater disagreement.
defer_for_first_pilot: Prompt-image alignment without a prompt-based product goal
AI-origin classifier as part of IQA
One scalar that silently averages quality, aesthetics and domain eligibility
useful_low_cost_auxiliary: Preserve known synthetic distortion parameters as provenance, not target quality.
Preserve existing VizWiz human defect votes.
Use brief structured defect evidence on a small audit set to detect teacher mistakes and style penalties; add full auxiliary training only after ablation.
Record labelled view hash, display/crop policy, assessor identity/version, rubric version and status as data provenance.
validation: Evaluate technical score against independent human technical ratings, not only aesthetics or broad VLM benchmarks.
Measure technical and aesthetic performance separately.
Include sharp-boring versus blurred-beautiful pairs, intentional blur, low-key/monochrome styles, readable diagrams, clean renders and authentic severe defects.
Choose whether to label aesthetics at scale only after human agreement and benefit to intended ranking are established.

recommendation.canonical_human_observation: One anchored integer grade1..5 per axis; technical quality first, aesthetics collected independently with its own anchors when required. Also an explicit unassessable/missing value, never a quality zero.
recommendation.aggregation: Retain every vote, per-image counts[1..5], n, mean and observed spread; fractional mean in[1,5] is derived, not another human response category. Do not round stored means to tenths. Display values can be rounded.
recommendation.teacher_observation: Store model/prompt/version/view and label_source. A teacher can emit one anchored grade; if retaining model-derived probabilities, mark them as model probabilities, not measured human-vote frequencies or confidence. Direct scalar scores are a competing pilot arm, not assumed better.
recommendation.display_mapping: 0..100 display may be25*(mean1to5-1). If1..100 is a product requirement use1+99*(mean1to5-1)/4. Either is an affine transform and adds no information.
recommendation.pairwise: Optional targeted supervision/evaluation with A_better/B_better/no_discernible_difference/cannot_assess, randomized presentation side. Tie-aware analysis required if ties are retained. Do not derive strict wins from any nonzero MOS gap without uncertainty checks.

metrics.labels: Human ordinal votes, empirical rating distributions, aggregate MOS, preference outcomes. MOS means mean opinion score; DMOS meaning/direction must be checked for each source.
metrics.score_models: PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS/DISTS are reference-based diagnostics; NIQE/BRISQUE are learned/statistical no-reference predictors. None are human labels just because they output a number.
metrics.model_evaluation: SRCC/SROCC tests ranking; Kendall tau-b handles ordinal concordance with ties; PLCC measures linear association but not absolute calibration; MAE/RMSE measure numeric error on a common declared scale.
plan: Primary held-out family-disjoint SRCC for technical quality and aesthetics separately, with source-family bootstrap intervals.
Report raw PLCC and calibrated MAE on the same scale. Fit any mapping on calibration/dev only, lock it before held-out evaluation; label benchmark-style post-fit PLCC separately.
Report per-source, per-defect, severity, content/style, and resolution slices; overall correlation can conceal failures.
Use held-out human pairwise agreement and probability calibration, split by same-content vs cross-content and near-tie cases. Check left/right order bias.
Use EMD/CDF distance only where empirical human-vote distributions exist and report number of raters.
Test quality-based filtering precision/recall at thresholds selected from use-case costs on development data; domain eligibility has separate metrics and does not enter photo-quality correlation.
Measure repeat-rater and split-half human reliability; do not call model disagreement confidence or a known human ceiling.

proposed_human_pilot.status: Planning proposal, not a literature-mandated minimum or sufficient-power claim.
proposed_human_pilot.design: Stratify photos across authentic and controlled defects, content/style and broad quality. Include attractive-but-defective and sharp-but-dull cases. Partition source families into calibration and held-out sets before selection. Five ratings are an initial screening budget; add raters for unstable means/distributions before treating them as gold. Present axes in separate randomized blocks to reduce anchoring.

recommendation.representation_decision_rule: Use one frozen encoder/student architecture and identical splits/views to compare scalar regression to mean, ordered/distributional target, and mean-plus-pairwise loss. Compare paired bootstrap deltas on held-out rank, calibrated error, filtering outcomes and defect slices. Prefer the simpler representation when uncertainty spans no practically relevant gain. Select thresholds and practical margins before opening final test results. Do not promise an arbitrary SRCC target.
